report.answer_text:
The Shape of Water (2017, directed by Guillermo del Toro) is a fantasy romance set in the early 1960s during the Cold War.
Setup: Elisa Esposito is a mute woman who works as a janitor at a secret U.S. government laboratory in Baltimore. She lives a quiet, lonely life. Her only close friends are her neighbor Giles, a closeted illustrator, and her coworker Zelda. One day, the lab receives a mysterious amphibious humanoid creature captured in South America, where locals worshipped it as a god. Colonel Richard Strickland, a cruel and ambitious security chief, is in charge of it. He torments the creature with a cattle prod.
Connection: Elisa secretly befriends the creature. She brings it food and music and teaches it some sign language. Because she communicates without speech, they form a deep bond that turns into love.
Conflict: The government plans to dissect the creature for research that could help the U.S. in the space race against the Soviets. A Soviet spy embedded at the lab, Dr. Robert Hoffstetler (whose real name is Dimitri), is also ordered to kill it to keep the U.S. from gaining an advantage. Hoffstetler sympathizes with the creature and hesitates.
Rescue: Elisa decides to free the creature. She recruits Giles and Zelda, and Hoffstetler also helps. They smuggle it out of the lab and hide it in Elisa's bathroom. There she floods the room so it can stay comfortable until it can be released into the ocean. Strickland becomes obsessed with finding it. He tortures information out of people and hunts down the conspirators.
Climax: Elisa and the creature reach the canal on the day of release, when the rain will let him return to the sea. Strickland arrives and shoots them both. The creature heals himself and kills Strickland. He then takes Elisa into the water. Her old scars on her neck turn out to be gills, and she comes back to life and becomes able to live underwater with him.
Themes: Love across differences, the treatment of outsiders (the mute, the gay, the Black, the "monstrous"), and who the real monsters are.
The film won four Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director.
